Lauren B. Peña

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 37, Travis County, Texas · Open seat

Founder and executive director of Peña Legal Advocacy (public-interest legal advocacy)

Lauren B. Peña is an Austin resident and public-interest advocate. She says she is a survivor of human trafficking and has testified before the Texas Legislature on welfare and housing policy. She came second in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for Texas' 37th Congressional District, then beat Ge'Nell Gary in the May 26 runoff with 58.2% of the vote, which made her the Republican nominee against incumbent Democrat Greg Casar.

Where Peña stands

Welfare reform
Calls welfare reform her top priority. Says the current system traps families in generational poverty and ends benefits all at once when income rises. Supports reforms that she says would save taxpayer money and reduce dependency.
Public safety and policing
Supports law enforcement. Proposes building trust between police and communities through education and community engagement, and bringing police critics together to discuss gang trends and systemic issues.
Housing and accessibility
Says Austin's elected Democrats have not responded to public housing residents' concerns, including accessibility for disabled and elderly residents. Has advocated before city officials and the Legislature for better housing conditions.
Government spending and taxes
Campaigns on an "America First: Faith, Family, Freedom" platform that she says would cut waste, reduce taxes and put effective policies in place.

Background

  • Republican nominee, U.S. House Texas District 37 (won primary runoff May 26, 2026); first run for office
  • Founder and Executive Director, Peña Legal Advocacy
  • Affiliated with the Austin Public Safety Commission, Austin Community Police Review Commission and Travis County Republican Party (per Ballotpedia)
  • B.A., Southern New Hampshire University (2024); attended University of Texas and Austin Community College (2023)
  • High school: Northwest High School; born in Harrisonburg, Virginia
